Facilities: the division (national seat) has a bathroom ban attached by the national legislature — in force there. Custody: national corrections bureau conversion therapy policies for inmates from 2026; immigration custody abuse. Those are for detainees — a visitor could end up in immigration custody. Threat framing: counterterrorism strategy lists "radically pro-transgender" groups; DOJ reward memorandum uses "radical gender ideology". Not directly a criterion, but contributes climate. Doesn't target individual trans visitors directly.

State facilities: broadly hostile at national level; local no ban of its own but national ban applies, local council cannot repeal.

Care services: national rules; hospitals subpoenaed for records of patients under 19 (residents). Emergency care discrimination not documented specifically.

Minors: executive order directing prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; care bans in 27 states; national health rules barring reimbursement. For a travelling minor, exposure is more indirect. Also state/province law invalidating documents.

0.35 anchors: denial of entry, invasive administrative review, no detention. That's worse than 0.35.

So arguably between 0.25 and 0.35. - Entry: documented detentions of foreign nationals over visa issues; case-note tagging; refusal where documents discrepant; possible lifetime fraud finding. This is a serious, traveller-facing, universal-ish exposure for outed trans travellers (marker mismatch).

Also, the trans-specific violence street level not documented.
